name: Qdrant
summary: A Rust vector database with strong filtering, quantisation and a licensing posture that suits self-hosters.
description:
Qdrant's pitch to engineers is control: payload filtering that runs during the search rather than after it, scalar and binary quantisation to fit more vectors in less RAM, sparse vectors for hybrid retrieval, and a real open-source build you can run on your own hardware without a sales call. Performance-per-byte is where it tends to win comparisons.

Like everything in this category, it solves storage and not retrieval quality — your chunking and embedding choices still decide whether answers are useful. Operating a database with replicas and backups is also a job someone has to want, which is the moment the managed cloud starts looking reasonable.
